newsitem.title: GERMANY: REUTERS GERMAN ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST - AUG 14.
newsitem.headline: REUTERS GERMAN ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST - AUG 14.

text.p: REUTERS GERMAN ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST
News from Reuters and the German press on Advertising, Marketing, Media, the Internet, Brand-name Products and Consumer Trends
ADVERTISING & MARKETING:

FRANKFURT - Digital television channel DF1 says it plans to introduce interactive advertising to viewers by the end of the month. The new technology will allow viewers to switch between various ads for a single product with the press of a button on a digital decoder box, sales director Nils Roehrig says. (Reuters)

BONN - O.Tel.O, a joint venture of the country's two largest utilities, Veba and RWE, will begin offering free phone calls to 5,000 people in Berlin in October in a a new service called "O.Tel.O-Spotline". The service broadcasts a short advertising spot before the call is completed and at regular intervals during the call. (Reuters)

FRANKFURT - Media experts call Germany's first television ad congress a success. Chief executive of the Media Center, Ulrich Bellieno says the congress gave smaller stations the bask in the attention normally only granted to the more established stations. (Reuters)

FRANKFURT - Media expert Ernstwilhelm Woehler says he sees companies gradually developing a negative impression of TV as an advertising medium. "Alternatives are being considered more seriously," Woehler says. He calls it counterproductive that TV stations's ad pricing policies are geared toward big customers. (Reuters)
MEDIA & THE INTERNET:

BONN - Apple Computer Inc shouldn't plan on using Europe as a springboard for a comeback in the personal computer business, a market research group say. International Data Corp estimates Apple's European unit shipments in the second quarter fell 31 percent from a year-ago, and its market share ranking fell to ninth place from fifth. (Reuters)

FRANKFURT - Private TV station Wetter Kanal (Weather Channel) says it plans to offer local forecasts for 100 cities and regions by the end of the year, up from 19.7 currently. Christian Boehmer, chief executive of Wetter und Reise Television GmbH & Co. KG. says the station hoped to boost ratings with more region-specific reports. (Reuters)
BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS & MARKETS:

BONN - Food giant Nestle says it has found no sign of contamination in groceries pulled from supermarket shelves across Germany after extortionists said they had poisoned its products. The extortionists said in a letter to the company they had poisoned products bearing the name of Nestle or its German subsidiary, Deutsche Thomy GmbH, in 55 stores in 14 cities. (Reuters)
BONN - A global consortium of 23 banks will place the German government's remaining 36 percent stake in airline Deutsche Lufthansa AG with investors, the Bonn transport ministry says. (Reuters)

STUTTGART - Gehe AG, a drug wholesaler says its newly acquired British unit Lloyds Chemists Plc is already well integrated and helped it post a 15.4 percent profit rise in the first half of 1997. (Reuters)

VIENNA - Leading German designer Hugo Boss tailored the much-feared brown and black uniforms of Hitler's Nazi elite during World War Two, Austrian current affairs magazine Profil says in its latest edition. The German men's fashion house, majority-owned by Italy's Marzotto group, said the report was probably accurate, although the company has no records or patterns from the wartime period. (Reuters)
PEOPLE NEWS:
WALLDORF - Claudia Knie is the new art director at the Frankfurt agency Trust. She was previously with the German Young & Rubicam agency. (Reuters)
